text:
customer_acme: Hey team — our app started getting garbled outputs after the failover yesterday. Lots of users reporting broken tokens and hallucinations. Request IDs attached: req_8f3a2a, req_8f3a2b. Any idea?

maya_support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you confirm which region the requests were intended for and the model id you passed?

customer_acme: We're targeting eu-west1 and we pass model: "redwood-alpha-1" in our client. We saw a sudden spike in latency and then a 502 for some requests. Logs show routing to us-central1 and model resolved as "redwood-alpha-1-quant" for some calls.

alex_oncall: @maya_support thanks — can you paste one raw request/response header pair (sanitized)? Need to know if the region header was set and what fallback happened.

customer_acme: pasted sample: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
  "prompt": "Summarize this...",
  "request_id": "req_8f3a2a"
}
```
Response headers: 
```
x-request-id: req_8f3a2a
x-served-region: us-central1
x-served-model: redwood-alpha-1-quant
x-latency-ms: 1280
```
Response body: tokens mangled, many � replacement characters, wrong token offsets.

jenna_eng_runtime: This looks like a cross-region fallback + incompatible model variant. Quantized variant has a different tokenizer/config mapping — that can cause garbled output if client expects alpha-1 vocab. Also latency >1s suggests route to cold infra.

sam_ml: Confirming: our quantized artifacts sometimes use different token IDs when we did hyperquant. We should never fall back to a different tokenizer family for the same model name. Need to see routing policy that allowed redwood-alpha-1 -> redwood-alpha-1-quant.

maya_support: @jenna_eng_runtime @sam_ml customer reports also saw billing spikes due to cross-region egress charges. @rachel_billing can you confirm unusual charge events tied to req_8f3a2a..b?

rachel_billing: I can see several cross-region egress records around 2026-04-16T09:12Z for customer_acme org (~$12 in a 40m window). I'll open a billing case and flag for credits pending incident resolution.

jenna_eng_runtime: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Set routing to prefer same-region and same-variant family (disable quantized fallback) — config flag: "allow_variant_fallback: false" per-tenant. 2) Short-term: pin model version in customer config to "redwood-alpha-1@v2026-03-10". 3) If they need low-latency, route to eu-west1 dedicated pool or spin up warm instances.

alex_oncall: Can you repro? Maya, please ask customer for a minimal curl repro that includes header X-Redwood-Region and model, and capture x-served-model header.

customer_acme: Here's a repro curl we ran: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \n -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west1" \n -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"hello","request_id":"req_8f3a2b"}'
```
We got x-served-region: us-central1 and x-served-model: redwood-alpha-1-quant

sam_ml: Thanks. That proves cross-region routing and variant fallback triggered. I'll check the variant mapping table and why quantized is considered compatible. Likely a metadata tag mismatch on the model catalog.

jenna_eng_runtime: @sam_ml also check router policy: if eu-west1 pool is saturated, router can fallback to any compatible family — somehow the compatibility comparator allowed alpha-1-quant. We should tighten comparator to require exact tokenizer signature match (vocab_checksum).

alex_oncall: For immediate customer relief I've pushed a per-tenant override to disallow variant fallback for customer_acme (allow_variant_fallback=false) and requested a warmup in eu-west1. Maya, can you confirm they see behavior change?

maya_support: Sent instructions and asked them to retry.

customer_acme: After your override, reran curl — now x-served-region: eu-west1 and x-served-model: redwood-alpha-1@v2026-03-10, latency 210ms, output looks correct. Thank you.

jenna_eng_runtime: Good. Postmortem action items: 1) Add tokenizer checksum to model metadata and require checksum equality for fallback. 2) Add alert when cross-region fallback increases >1% for a region in 15m. 3) Add billing telemetry link for per-request egress to make support triage faster.

sam_ml: I'm going to run a scan across catalog to find other models where tokenizer checksums differ between variants and create a migration plan.

alex_oncall: Creating an incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime (priority P2) and eng-ml for the tokenizer mismatch. Incident ID: INC-2026-0428-07. I'll put timeline + customer impact in the ticket.

deploy_bot: Deploy scheduled: routing-policy-fix -> staging in 10m (by jenna_eng_runtime).

maya_support: Customer confirmed resolution. Closing support thread but keeping incident open until fixes complete. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

acs_incident_bot: Incident INC-2026-0428-07 created and assigned to eng-runtime, eng-ml.

rachel_billing: Billing case opened (BILL-9241) and provisional credit requested for customer_acme.

alex_oncall: Final note: customers can pin exact model versions to avoid variant fallbacks. Documented workaround: add header `X-Redwood-Model-Version: vYYYY-MM-DD` or set `allow_variant_fallback=false` in tenant config.

customer_acme: Great, appreciate the quick turnaround.
